payload.title: Australia Real Weddings From Coast to Country
payload.meta_title: Australia Real Weddings From Coast to Country
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with AUD 150k or more to spend who are weighing a wedding at home against one abroad, and want to see real Australian weddings by setting (coast and beach, country and vineyard, city, garden, island and reef) before choosing a region, along with the questions to ask a venue and the legal first step for marrying in Australia.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor (one click to the Wedded Concierge page), with the magazine as the early stage lead magnet secondary.
payload.angle: Page one for Australian real weddings is mostly directory galleries and vendor showcases. This page gathers only the Australian weddings we have published ourselves, groups them by the kind of setting a couple is actually choosing between (coast and beach, country and vineyard, city, garden, island and reef), introduces each couple by the names their story uses, and describes the setting without selling a venue. It then turns what those weddings share into questions to put to any Australian venue, and gives the plain legal first step (the Notice of Intended Marriage and who can marry you) from our own guides, so a couple can move from looking to planning on one page.

sections.heading: Australia real weddings in brief
sections.brief: Direct answer in 2 to 3 sentences: these are real weddings held in Australia that we have published, grouped by setting, each linked to the couple's full story, followed by the questions they raise for a venue and the legal first step for marrying here. State the number of featured stories only once the SEO map fixes it. Link the /blog/real-weddings hub once here. Then a separate 'Key takeaways' heading with exactly 4 takeaways, each one sentence: (1) every wedding below comes from our own published stories, grouped by setting and linked to the full account; (2) one concrete lesson the cards share, phrased as what to ask a venue (writer chooses from section 3 once cards are fixed); (3) the legal first step, that a Notice of Intended Marriage is lodged with your celebrant within the window set out in our NOIM guide (reuse the pack fact only, no new figure); (4) a Wedded Advisor can plan a wedding anywhere in Australia or abroad and quotes in AUD for Australian couples. Exactly one sentence each, no colons.

sections.heading: Real weddings by setting
sections.brief: Group cards under H3 setting headings, for example 'Coast and beach weddings', 'Country and vineyard weddings', 'City weddings', 'Garden weddings', 'Island and reef weddings'. Use only settings the SEO map fills; merge or drop an empty group rather than leave it thin, and never pad a group with a story from outside Australia. One short card per story from 02-seo.json's real wedding map (aim 8 to 12): the couple's names exactly as the published story names them (H4 or bold lead, writer to follow the garden facet pattern), the setting described without the venue name (for example 'a headland above the beach', 'a vineyard estate', 'a harbourside room'), the state or region only where the story names it, one or two details the story itself states in our own words, and one link to the story. Reuse the garden facet's Australian cards (Kristyn and Damien, Paige and Todd, Helen and Trent, and Samira and Tom only if the SEO step confirms Australia) with the same names and links, rewording so the two facets do not share sentences. Skip paid client features and any wedding not held in Australia. Nothing added beyond each story: no dates, guest counts, vendors, labels, venue names or budgets unless the story states them, and never venue or vendor names even when it does. Link /real-weddings/beach-wedding from the coast and beach group and the garden facet from the garden group (garden facet is a draft, so <!-- LINK: /real-weddings/garden-wedding when live --> unless the SEO step finds it live).

sections.heading: What these weddings share and what to ask your venue
sections.brief: 3 to 5 planning lessons drawn from patterns across the cards (for example a ceremony and reception in different spaces, an outdoor ceremony, guests travelling to a regional or island setting, a marquee or styled space the couple dressed themselves). Each lesson is written as questions for the venue, with one line of why, never as a claim about any couple's day or what worked for them. Never state a venue's rule, capacity, curfew or wet weather space as fact. The Concierge primary CTA sits before this section or within its first lines (anchor 'Wedded Concierge'). The magazine magnet link goes at the end of this section (/magazine with UTM; anchor must not say free).

sections.heading: Planning a wedding in Australia from here
sections.brief: Short, practical. Legal line: to marry legally in Australia you give a Notice of Intended Marriage to your celebrant, linking /expert-advice/notice-of-intended-marriage-explained-step-by-step, and an authorised celebrant or minister of religion performs the ceremony, linking /expert-advice/who-can-perform-a-marriage. Reuse legal facts only from the notice-of-intended-marriage, who-can-perform-a-marriage and marriage-licence packs via batch au_a; no new legal claims. Seasons and weather only if a BoM fact is already in an existing pack (for example the Oceania or Hamilton Island batch) and is linked at the claim; otherwise write weather as questions for the venue (what the covered option is, who makes the call and when). Regional travel for guests as questions (how guests reach the setting, where they stay). Link Australian guides only where they fit and the SEO step confirms them live and suitable: the Whitsundays island guide, /best-wedding-spots-in-byron-bay (anchor must not say best) and a Sydney guide that names no venues; skip old Sydney venue lists that name venues. The single body Wedded Advisor line sits here with the Concierge secondary CTA: a Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.

sections.heading: Australia real wedding FAQ
sections.brief: 4 to 6 questions (questions allowed here only), for example: Where can I see real weddings held in Australia? Do I need a Notice of Intended Marriage to marry in Australia? Who can legally marry us in Australia? What should we ask an Australian venue about the weather? Can a Wedded Advisor plan a wedding in Australia? Answers repeat body content only, no new claims, no figures beyond the NOIM pack.

Then the closing CTA with the anchor 'Wedded Concierge'.
